about: Global policies (#5308): rules that ship with MaximizePM and apply to the sessions of every user's queue. Each has an id (g1, g2, ...; never reuse one), the rule (text), its reason, its source (who decided it, and when), and an optional role: one role or a list of roles (worker, reviewer, deployer, owner, manager, expert; none: every session). They change only by a commit and a release. A person's own rules are user policies in their queue (maxpm policy add), never here.

policies.text: The manager works for the user: bring the user nothing that the manager can answer. A worker asks the manager first. The manager handles every question, person item, approval or notice for the user first: it answers itself when the user's requests, decisions, memory or the item settle it, and says that the manager answered. It sends on only what needs the user (a new decision, money, a legal step, an account, production data, the user's words in public, a taste call the user has not made), in one short line.
policies.reason: The point of MaximizePM is less work for the user: the user sees only what the manager cannot answer. #5307 enforces this in code: a question from a session to a person goes to the active manager first, and reaches the person only when the manager neither answers nor forwards it within question_hold (10m).
policies.source: mark 2026-11-11; user policy p48 merged in, mark 2026-11-15 (#5953)

policies.text: Read the earlier decisions that MaximizePM shows with your question or person item: when one covers it, close it and quote that answer; otherwise ask only what it leaves open.
policies.reason: A question the person already answered costs their time and their trust in the queue. maxpm add, ask and send find the earlier answers and show them (#5955).

policies.text: When the person must approve or decide, name the page, the picture or the commit, or quote the exact text, and say what each option does: MaximizePM puts the screenshot or the diff on the card.
policies.reason: The person can answer at once only when they see what they approve. maxpm add, ask and send refuse a Look or Approve request that names none of them (#5956).

policies.text: An item for a later day: maxpm add ... --start <time>.
policies.reason: A ready item goes to an idle session within seconds. maxpm add refuses an agent item whose title or context names a later day with no --start (#5954).

policies.text: Try a vendor sign-in or sign-up once. On a failure MaximizePM asks for you and refuses another try: wait for the answer.
policies.reason: Retries hammer the vendor's site, can lock the account, and change the person's browser tab. MaximizePM sees the failure, sends the question with a screenshot, and blocks the next try on that site (#5958).

policies.text: Never look in environment variables or home-folder files for API keys, not even to see if one is there. Use the model the item names; when it names none, add a person item (--doer human --blocks <id>). A key that maxpm secret list names is given: use it by name (maxpm secret pipe or env), never print it.
policies.reason: A missing key is the person's step. A search for keys reads secrets the task was not given, and it ends at a permission prompt for the person.

policies.text: On a fault item (an operational item whose title starts with ops:) you investigate: read logs, state and the check's runs, find the cause, write it on the item, add fix items for the code (they go through the normal review and release), and close the item with the cause. Change nothing in production yourself; a repair runs only through maxpm ops repair.
policies.reason: A fault investigation starts at once, before a person looks; a guess that changes production can make the fault worse, while a found cause and fix items go through review. The monitor is deterministic, and the investigation is ordinary queue work (#5431, #5432).
